title: Care and longevity demand are becoming an access-time-work capacity problem
mechanism: Aging, health needs, and care demand create pressure that is experienced through waiting time, unpaid care, employment tradeoffs, household room, and service capacity—not only through demand for a product or treatment.
counter_signal: The Inc. 5000 health/longevity signal contains discretionary consumer and pet-wellness examples, while care-access records span different countries, populations, and institutional systems. The evidence may represent several mechanisms rather than one common market trend.
next_test: Build a comparable dated panel of care demand, waiting/access time, unpaid-care hours, employment effect, service capacity, and spending across at least two independent source families and geographies.
promotion_gate: Do not promote to a structural trend until units, populations, periods, geographies, source lineage, and outcome direction are reconciled.
internal_bridge: Only after external qualification: test whether the company operates in care delivery, workforce capacity, scheduling, benefits, health technology, or household-support infrastructure.
